summary: The three singletons BSP_Game_EnterFrontEndShell builds into 00E198B8, 00E198AC and 00E198B4 are three derivations of one base class (constructor 00684E10). The base carries two 1Ch-byte interface-request records at +04h and +20h, a bool at +3Ch and membership in a std::map of every manager at 00E19898. Drain requests 16h, 06h and 09h do not destroy anything: each calls virtual +0Ch, which is the shared deactivate 00683AA0, so the object, its screens and both records survive.

drain_requests.why_individual: Activate (00684700) already deactivates every other registered manager, so the only thing a caller can ask for that Activate does not provide is lowering one manager and raising nothing. One request per manager lets the drain name the one it means. What must survive is the pending record at +20h/+38h: 00684700 replays it when the manager comes back, so freeing anything in +0Ch would leave nothing to show.

follow_up_packets.contract: The two zero-terminated varargs screen-set calls every Activate and every +10h override makes, the jump table at 006873EC, and what an empty list does to the 95-slot screen registry.
What raises the 00E19894 lock that blocks every in-session HUD interface, and why id 2Ch is exempt.
The seven objects at 00E198AC+58h..+70h, which interface id each serves, and the one the shell drives through 005884A0.
The six objects at 00E198B4+40h..+54h, the unidentified +58h member and the vector at +5Ch, and the online refresh 00689510 gates on.
The std::map at 00E19898 keyed by manager pointer, its node layout, and whether anything other than 00684700 iterates it.
